articles.title: Another 'miracle' in Istanbul - but this one hurt Liverpool
articles.summary: Liverpool conceded "cheap" and "messy" goals in their defeat by Fenerbahce, says boss Andoni Iraola, as former Reds hero Dirk Kuyt celebrates a "miracle" in...
articles.body:
When it comes to comebacks, Liverpool and Istanbul have plenty of history - but this time Andoni Iraola's side made the wrong kind.

Having hit the front for a second time against Fenerbahce, when Alexander Isak nodded in after 69 minutes, Liverpool were seemingly on their way to a thoroughly impressive away win.

But Iraola's players then capitulated amid a febrile atmosphere, as spirited hosts led by interim boss Dirk Kuyt - a Liverpool hero of years gone by - pulled off a shock Champions League comeback victory.

By losing 3-2 at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium, Iraola's visitors created that unwanted slice of history: this was the latest Liverpool have ever gone ahead in a major European game and then been beaten.

Iraola described the goals they conceded as "cheap" and "messy".

After Liverpool let three points slip from their grasp, Kuyt spoke of how he had encouraged Fenerbahce's players to embrace the never-say-die mindset that allowed the Reds to achieve so many great feats in Europe in the past.

He joined Liverpool in 2006, a year after the team's famous 'Miracle of Istanbul' comeback in the Champions League final, and spent six years as a first-team fixture.

"We told each other to stick together and be united. That's something I learned from Liverpool, who we played against," Kuyt said. "We made a miracle tonight - not many expected us to win."

He and Fenerbahce will remember this one for a long time. Liverpool will want to quickly forget it.

After winning five games in a row, Iraola's side have gone on to lose twice in four days. Arsenal on Sunday, and now this.

On the flight back from Istanbul, there will be plenty of disappointment at the way in which Liverpool failed to see this game out.

"It's frustration because it's a difficult place to come and play," said Iraola. "We were, during most part of the game, thinking we can win this one. But obviously it hasn't happened."

All three of Fenerbahce's goals came from set-pieces.

Former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood benefited from a slice of luck when his free-kick deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet in the first half for Fenerbahce's first equaliser, and Liverpool only had themselves to blame when Cody Gakpo's header took the ball past Alisson and gave Birmingham-born Archie Brown a tap in to make it 2-2.

Six minutes later, Liverpool made a mess of Brown's looping ball in the box and Vedat Muriqi beat three players in red and headed past Alisson.

"They are cheap goals. They are messy goals," said Iraola.

"It's a free-kick. It's quite far also and it's through the wall.

"Mistakes can cost you. For the last goal, it's a long throw and the first phase is controlled but after a very long ball, Muriqi wins it.

"The second goal, Cody is the one touching the ball just in front of Ali [Alisson].

"In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate because it was so noisy. It was even difficult for me to give any kind of instruction. I suppose the communication between Ali and Cody was difficult."

'They look like they can concede at any moment'

After showing signs of genuine progress in recent weeks, Liverpool let potential victory slip away here in a concerning manner.

Trey Nyoni's first goal for the club had given them an early lead, but the teenager's deflected strike was cancelled out by Greenwood's reply in kind four minutes later.

The real drama came from the 69th minute to the 79th, with Liverpool inching ahead again, close to a fourth win in four in the competition, but unable to see the job through.

"It feels like a step back from what we saw against Arsenal because everyone thought, OK, we are seeing huge improvements from Liverpool," said ex-Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock, who was watching the game for Match of the Day.

"It was a much-changed team. However, the simple mistakes that they made from set-pieces or simple balls into the box are not good enough.

"The frustrating part for Liverpool fans is that we all know what the problems are. So, where is the solution? That's what Iraola is trying to do at the moment, but it's just a question of how long it takes.

"The biggest issue is that this keeps on happening, with Liverpool looking like they can concede at any moment and being so open on the counter-attack. There is a repetitive theme of the goals they are conceding and it undoes all the good work they do when they go forward.

"When you go ahead, twice, away from home at Fenerbahce in the Champions League then, if that is Arsenal they win that game - they see it out against a team like Fenerbahce.

"Liverpool don't have the ability to do that at the moment, and that is what is really frustrating."

'We showed Europe how big Fenerbahce is'

On the eve of this game in the Kadikoy neighbourhood of Istanbul, Kuyt spoke passionately about how Fenerbahce had the opportunity to show Europe their true colours.

He will step aside now, with former Newcastle player Emre Belozoglu taking over as head coach officially from Thursday.

Thanks to this night, Europe now knows all about Fenerbahce.

They have had a torrid season so far, though, having lost four of their 10 league games and taken a 6-0 drubbing at Aston Villa on their travels outside Turkey, but Kuyt's men delivered a performance that will live long in the memory for anyone associated with the club.

"We showed Europe how big Fenerbahce is. This is what the spirit of this side is," said Kuyt.

"I think it's very special that for the first time since 18 years, Fenerbahce win a game against [an English side].

"Some people will remember but the number on the back of my shirt was 18 in Liverpool. So that's something really special for me in person.

"I said exactly the same thing to the players before the game. Although we are in a very difficult situation, we have a chance to bring another miracle in Istanbul. And if you get that miracle, things can change in a positive way."

They delivered in style, with 24-year-old former Derby County prospect Brown getting a goal and an assist in the second half.

"The Champions League is a great opportunity for Archie to show himself," said Kuyt.

"It's well known how good a player he is in Turkey. He did a fantastic job today. His defence and attack were very good. I'm very pleased with his performance, I'm pleased with the performance of all my players.

"It's a very special night for everyone who loves Fenerbahce."

articles.title: Cesc Fabregas' Como equal Champions League record with landmark win at Lens
articles.summary: Cesc Fabregas' Serie A side Como have made UEFA Champions League history after a stunning win at Lens, just weeks after beating Premier League giants Manches...
articles.body:
Cesc Fabregas' Como etched their name into UEFA Champions League history with a stunning 9-1 demolition of Lens, as their remarkable European adventure continues to gather momentum.

The Italian club is competing in the tournament for the very first time, yet have shown no signs of being intimidated. Following a meteoric rise through the ranks in recent seasons, they delivered a ruthless performance on French soil Wednesday night.

With three wins from four matches, Como sit fourth in the league phase at the halfway point - ahead of heavyweights such as Barcelona, Manchester City, Liverpool and Bayern Munich.

Just weeks after dismantling Manchester United, Como have reached new heights, with their victory in France matching the largest winning margin ever recorded in Champions League history, as per The Mirror .

Liverpool's 8-0 triumph over Beşiktaş in 2007 and Real Madrid's identical scoreline against Malmö in 2015 had previously stood as the competition's most commanding victories. Como have now joined that exclusive list - and unlike the Reds and Real, they achieved it on the road.

Fabregas' men were firmly in control at 3-0 up at the break, with Anastasios Douvikas netting twice before the interval. He completed his hat-trick in the second half as the Italians piled on six additional goals.

Nico Paz and Lucas Da Cunha were among the scorers in a remarkable display that saw seven different players get on the scoresheet. Currently sitting fourth in Serie A, Como will face AEK Athens and Real Betis before the year concludes, by which point they may have already secured their spot in the knockout rounds.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

They will then have the opportunity to cement their reputation with their remaining two fixtures against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.

Fabregas admitted following their 4-1 victory over the Red Devils that he had second thoughts about instructing his squad to take their foot off the gas despite their overwhelming dominance.

"I have some regrets over the last 10 minutes maybe," the Spaniard later said. "I was actually saying to the team to 'slow the tempo, because we have another game coming up'."

Como's tally of 19 goals across four Champions League matches is bettered only by defending champions PSG, who have netted 20 times in European competition so far this season.

articles.title: Miami football releases statement after Malachi Toney suffers ankle injury at practice
articles.summary: Miami football released a statement Wednesday after star wide receiver Malachi Toney suffered an injury at practice ahead of Saturday’s matchup at Notre Dame...
articles.body:
Miami football released a statement Wednesday after star wide receiver Malachi Toney suffered an injury at practice ahead of Saturday's matchup at Notre Dame.

The sophomore has recorded 73 receptions for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns this season, leading Power 4 receivers in catches. His production has helped the Hurricanes reach 8-0 and claim the No. 1 spot in the College Football Playoff rankings.

Miami faces a 7-1 Notre Dame team ranked No. 11 in the CFP standings, with Toney's availability drawing attention ahead of the road game.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

NBC Sports's Nicole Auerbach shared Miami Athletics' statement Wednesday on X, formerly Twitter, following the initial injury reports.

"Malachi Toney sustained an injury during Wednesday's practice and is currently undergoing further evaluation by the team's medical staff. We will share additional updates as appropriate."

Toney accounts for 35.1% of the Hurricanes' receptions, 38.6% of their receiving yards and 46.4% of their touchdown catches, underscoring his importance to quarterback Darian Mensah's offense.

The receiver has dealt with ankle issues this season without missing a game, briefly exiting against Wake Forest, Clemson, and Florida State. The Hurricanes statement did not specify the nature of Wednesday's injury or establish a return timetable.

Toney made his college debut against Notre Dame last year, recording six catches for 82 yards and a touchdown in Miami's 27-24 victory. That result helped the Hurricanes secure the final at-large CFP berth while leaving the Irish outside the field.

Saturday's rematch kicks off at 7:30 p.m. ET at Notre Dame Stadium in South Bend. The Hurricanes have not announced whether their standout receiver will be available as they pursue a ninth straight victory and look to strengthen their College Football Playoff position.

articles.title: Cape Verde captain Ryan Mendes cleared after sexual assault allegations
articles.summary: Allegations against Ryan Mendes were reported during the World Cup, but police in now say the accuser will be charged with making a false statement.
articles.body:
Cape Verde player Ryan Mendes will not be charged with rape after an investigation in New Zealand cleared the midfielder, his lawyer said.

Accusations that Mendes had sexually assaulted a Brazilian translator working with the group during a trip to New Zealand were first reported during the World Cup . Cape Verde, a country of fewer than 500,000 people off the coast of Western Africa, was on a fairy tale run, avoiding defeat against Spain, Uruguay and Saudi Arabia to move into the knockout stages.

Cape Verde manager Bubista, who now coaches the Moroccan club where Mendes plays, refused to answer questions about the allegations ahead of a Round of 32 meeting with Argentina. Mendes captained Cape Verde in that match, a heroic performance that saw the Blue Sharks push the eventual runners-up to extra time before falling, 3-2 .

Cape Verde's dramatic World Cup debut against Spain captured in photos

After a civil claim and an investigation by police in New Zealand, Mendes' lawyer Karl Trotter said the 36-year-old has been cleared.

"The New Zealand Police have advised counsel in writing that they have concluded their investigation of the matter and Mr Mendes will not be facing charges. Today, and in connection with this matter, the police have charged a female pursuant to s. 111 Crimes Act 1961, with making a false statement," Trotter said in a statement released Nov. 4. "It is to be hoped that this recent turn of events, clearing Mr. Mendes of the allegation of rape, attracts the same level of media attention as the original reporting."

Police in New Zealand confirmed to local media outlets that the woman is expected in court to answer the charges of making a false statement.

"A decision to prosecute in these circumstances is not taken lightly and follows months of investigative work by our Adult Sexual Assault Team," Detective Inspector Scott Beard said .

Despite their strong showing at the World Cup, Cape Verde fell in both of its first two games after the tournament, African Cup of Nations qualification matches against Mali and Rwanda. Mendes was in the starting lineup for both of those games and has been recalled for back-to-back matches with Liberia this month.

articles.title: Todd McShay Predicts Arch Manning Will Forgo 2027 NFL Draft Amid Up-And-Down Season at Texas
articles.summary: Heading into the 2026 college football season, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was expected to be the next generational quarterback prospect and the consensus No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. After eight games, one NFL draft analyst expects the legacy quarterback won't hear his name called at all next April.
articles.body:
Heading into the 2026 college football season, Texas quarterback Arch Manning was expected to be the next generational quarterback prospect and the consensus No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. After eight games, one NFL draft analyst expects the legacy quarterback won't hear his name called at all next April.

The Ringer's Todd McShay believes Manning will return for another collegiate season, regardless of whether he's at Texas or elsewhere.

"I think Arch is coming back to school next year, and I think he should," McShay said during a recent appearance on Yahoo Sports Daily . "Whether he's at Texas or not is a conversation for another time. ... I like the villain version of Arch, where it's a little bit more [of] take the ball, three-step drop, top of the drop, trust your eyes, let it rip."

The early portion of the season appeared to be going as planned for Manning, who guided the Longhorns to the No. 1 rank through the first four games. Then, Texas dropped two consecutive games against unranked Oklahoma and Florida. The losses resulted in heightened scrutiny of Manning's flaws, and head coach Steve Sarkisian even seemed open to the possibility of making a change at the starting quarterback spot.

Manning has faced questions about his decision-making and consistency throughout an up-and-down campaign. The 22-year-old quarterback has taken more sacks through eight games than he did throughout the entire 2025 season, and his seven interceptions are already tied with his total from last season. Injuries have taken a toll on the Longhorns' offensive line, but Manning deserves his fair share of culpability for the sacks.

Despite the struggles, Manning still has an opportunity to get back on track. Texas is ranked No. 7 and has two upcoming games against ranked opponents, No. 18 Missouri and No. 14 LSU. Manning can still make a run for the national championship — and the 2027 NFL Draft — but the margin for error is slim.

articles.title: Miami WR Malachi Toney will reportedly undergo ankle surgery, eyeing return for College Football Playoff
articles.summary: Malachi Toney has 73 catches for 1,027 receiving yards and 13 TDs.
articles.body:
Miami will be without Malachi Toney against Notre Dame, and perhaps the rest of the regular season.

Toney suffered an ankle injury in practice on Wednesday and will now miss out on the No. 1 Hurricanes' trip to South Bend. Toney is set to undergo surgery due to the injury, according to Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger .

A specific timeline isn't known yet, but the belief is that Toney will be out between four to six weeks. That would make it possible for him to return for the College Football Playoff. The first round games in the postseason are set to take place on Dec. 18-19, and the quarterfinals are scheduled for Dec. 30 and New Year's Day.

Toney is second among all receivers in college football with 73 catches and is one of only three players with more than 1,000 receiving yards. His 13 receiving touchdowns are only behind Oregon State WR Jesse Legree's 14 TD catches.

Entering Week 10, Toney's odds to win the Heisman Trophy at BetMGM were +325 and only behind teammate Darian Mensah (+150) and Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith (+275).

The sophomore is averaging nearly 130 yards a game for the No. 1 Hurricanes as Miami is one of just three unbeaten teams remaining in college football. The Hurricanes are 6.5-point underdogs at No. 11 Notre Dame on Saturday night, as the Irish are seven spots lower in the CFP rankings than they are in the AP Top 25.

That position makes the game a potential must-win for Notre Dame's playoff hopes given its remaining schedule features Boston College, SMU and Syracuse. A year ago, Notre Dame missed the playoff at 10-2 largely because of a Week 1 loss to Miami. The Fighting Irish were ahead of the Hurricanes in all but the final iteration of the CFP rankings. Even though neither team played on conference championship weekend, Miami leapfrogged Notre Dame to make the College Football Playoff and subsequently advanced to the national championship game.

Toney would have been matched up against star Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore on Saturday, had he been able to go. The potential top-five pick in the 2027 NFL Draft missed the Irish's Week 9 win over Navy, but is expected to return on Saturday.

But now, the Hurricanes will have to find a way to both win in South Bend, and keep their playoff position intact, without Toney available.

articles.title: Latest Heisman Trophy Odds for Jeremiah Smith, Darian Mensah, More After Malachi Toney Injury Update
articles.summary: Malachi Toney's Heisman hopes likely came to a close on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Malachi Toney's Heisman hopes likely came to a close on Wednesday.

The Miami wideout, following news that that he'll will surgery on his injured ankle and is potentially facing four weeks or more on the sidelines, no longer ranks among FanDuel's top favorites for the award.

Instead, Ohio State wideout Jeremiah Smith (+160), Toney's teammate Darian Mensah (+165), Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr (+550), Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (+950) and LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt (+3500) are currently the frontrunners.

Just last week, Toney was No. 3 in the odds for the award. But Miami announced Wednesday that he "sustained an injury during Wednesday's practice and is currently undergoing further evaluation by the team's medical staff. We will share additional updates as appropriate."

Per multiple reports, he's dealing with a high-ankle sprain that will likely end his regular season and seemingly keep him out until the College Football Playoff should Miami qualify.

The undefeated and top-ranked Hurricanes (8-0) still have Notre Dame, Duke, Virginia Tech and Boston College on the schedule, alongside a potential berth in the ACC Championship Game. Being without Toney, one of the most electric playmakers in the sport, won't make running the table easy.

Toney has registered 73 catches for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns this season. He's been awesome.

But so has the man throwing him the ball. Mensah has 2,425 passing yards, 25 touchdowns and just one interception on the season, adding another two scores on the ground.

Perhaps nobody has been more impressive than Ohio State's Smith, however. The Buckeyes' superstar has 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns, numbers that are going to look ridiculous by the time the season is over.

Smith and Mensah have a pretty wide gulf on the field at the moment, though Carr is making his case, throwing for 1,849 yards, 18 touchdowns and a pick while rushing for three scores.

If Notre Dame upsets Miami on Saturday and Carr has a big game, the odds will likely fluctuate in a significant way.

articles.title: Top-ranked Miami faces nightmare injury concern as star receiver Malachi Toney set to undergo ankle surgery
articles.summary: Notre Dame needs a signature win to climb the CFP rankings, but the Malachi Toney ankle injury adds a new wrinkle to Saturday's Miami showdown.
articles.body: Miami's highly anticipated showdown against Notre Dame on Saturday night had another layer added to the storylines on Wednesday, as the health of Heisman Trophy contender Malachi Toney will now linger over the next month. The No. 1 Hurricanes were already underdogs heading into the matchup in South Bend, but now head coach Mario Cristobal will be without his top playmaker on offense besides quarterback Darian Mensah. During practice on Wednesday, Malachi Toney suffered an injury to his ankle that forced the wide receiver to leave practice and head straight to a local facility to be evaluated for what could be a massive hit to the Hurricanes' national title hopes. CFP RANKINGS: NOTRE DAME FACES SUDDEN DEATH, SEC FEELING GOOD, AND BIG TEN CLOSE TO HITTING THE PANIC BUTTON While there was some optimism earlier in the afternoon that this could end up being an injury that doesn’t keep Toney off the field on Saturday night, there was obviously growing concern later on in the day that this could potentially keep Malachi off the field for an extended period of time. "Malachi Toney sustained an injury during Wednesday’s practice and is currently undergoing further evaluation by the team’s medical staff," Miami said in a statement earlier on Wednesday. "We will share additional updates as appropriate." Now, the star wide receiver will undergo surgery on his ankle, after an MRI and X-ray were done on Wednesday evening, as CBS Sports first reported. Toney suffered a high-ankle sprain, according to sources, and will undergo the infamous "TightRope" surgery that Miami is hoping will have the star wide receiver return for the College Football Playoff in four to six weeks. But, this is obviously a "hopeful" mindset by Miami football officials. Multiple gambling establishments had already bumped Notre Dame from 5-point favorites to 6.5-point favorites by Wednesday evening. All eyes on Miami, as Heisman Trophy candidate could play major factor in CFP rankings The health of Malachi Toney will be one of the most talked about subjects over the next month, given the initial CFP rankings that were released on Tuesday night. Following the win last weekend against North Carolina, the Miami wide receiver has now accounted for 1,027 yards receiving, with 13 touchdowns on 73 receptions. What does this Hurricanes offense look like without its star wide receiver? We're about to find out, given the unfortunate news that he will be undergoing surgery. Just like any other player at this time, Toney was dealing with the type on bumps and bruises you would expect eight games into the season. If the Hurricanes were to lose on Saturday night without Malachi on the field, the subsequent three weeks would be interesting to watch unfold from a rankings standpoint. OHIO STATE'S NATIONAL TITLE HOPES ARE RIGHTFULLY FADING AFTER USC DELIVERS REALITY CHECK IN SHOCKING UPSET What would the committee have to say when it comes to Miami not having a Heisman Trophy candidate on the field if the injury were to keep Toney out for at least a few weeks? Notre Dame faces what could be a must-win game in the CFP committee’s eyes On the other side, this is setting up to be a pivotal game for Notre Dame after being ranked 11th in the first CFP poll of 2026. There is no sugarcoating the fact that the Fighting Irish do not have a signature win this season, and their strength of schedule leaves much to be desired. BYU is the only ranked team they have played that appears in the College Football Playoff top 25. "But when you look at Notre Dame’s schedule and the wins that they have, vs. the teams that are ahead of them, they don’t have that signature win right now. They lost in their only Top-25 matchup at BYU. The next best win as on a neutral site against Wisconsin," CFP chairman Hunter Yurachek noted. "They’ve a great opportunity in front of them this weekend at home vs. Miami to get that signature win that I think they need to move up in the rankings. But the committee is very impressed by them. They wouldn’t be 11th if we were not." Just when you thought Notre Dame's college football playoff standings would be the main storyline heading into Saturday’s showdown, we are now paying attention to see how Miami responds without its Heisman Trophy candidate.

articles.summary: "Es un partido en el que la sensación era que sin necesitábamos meter más, metemos más"
articles.body: José Mourinho se pronuncia en rueda de prensa, tras el partido que el Real Madrid ganó 2-3 al AEK de Atenas en Champions League, sobre la polémica del "penaltito" de Kylian Mbappé en Santander en encuentro de LaLiga en el que el Madrid se impuso 0-3. Tiempo de Revisión reconoció el error en el penalti de Mbappé en Santander, considerando que hay un error de Munuera Montero en el campo y también del VAR por no intervenir. "Estamos hablando de un penaltito… A mí lo que me parece es que es una situación que no tiene consecuencia en puntos. Es un partido que si no tenemos ese penalti ganamos igual de tres, cuatro o cinco. Es un partido en el que la sensación era que si necesitábamos meter más, metemos más. Y la sensación es que en el segundo tiempo el equipo no ha querido más", apuntó el técnico luso sobre el discutido penalti que se le pitó a Mbappé en El Sardinero. Mou insistió en que "estamos hablando de un penaltito, te confieso. Es el tipo de penalti que para mí el árbitro pita penalti pensando al 100% que es penalti, por la dimensión de la acción". "Para mí es penalti, pero te digo... Si me lo pitan en contra no estoy contento, y por ello ya podemos ver que es un penaltito", subrayó. El técnico del Madrid destacó que "estamos hablando de un partido que no tiene historia. ¿De qué estamos hablando? De un partido que podemos meter cinco y hemos tenido un penalti que crea algún tipo de duda". "Atentos que hay partidos en este campeonato donde penaltis, decisiones, expulsiones tiene un gran impacto en el resultado. En este, impacto cero", sentenció.

articles.title: El Como hace historia: todos los récords que ha pulverizado
articles.standfirst: El arranque en la Champions League del equipo de Cesc Fàbregas ya es de leyenda
articles.summary: El arranque en la Champions League del equipo de Cesc Fàbregas ya es de leyenda
articles.body: Si la clasificación para la competición lograda la pasada temporada ya fue histórica para un club que hace apenas seis campañas militaba en la tercera categoría del fútbol italiano, el arranque en la Champions League del Como de Cesc Fàbregas ya es de leyenda. En una noche inolvidable para todo el fútbol italiano, el conjunto lombardo goleó por 9-1, se colocó provisionalmente en la cuarta posición -la misma que ocupa en la Serie A- y se convirtió en el segundo equipo más goleador de la Champions: 19 goles en cuatro partidos. Cuatro al Leipzig, cuatro al Manchester United, uno al Feyenoord y nueve al Lens. Solo el PSG de Luis Enrique ha marcado más. Pero centrémonos en la noche de Lens. Para entender la magnitud de la hazaña protagonizada por los chicos de Cesc, basta con repasar los récords que han batido. Para empezar, el Como se convirtió en el primer equipo italiano de la historia de la Copa de Europa/UEFA Champions League en marcar al menos siete goles a domicilio. Aunque quizá no conocían los detalles del récord y decidieron llegar hasta los nueve. A nivel europeo, igualó el registro del Bayern de Múnich, que se impuso por 9-2 al Dinamo de Zagreb el 17 de septiembre de 2024, y se convirtió en el equipo que ha logrado la victoria más abultada a domicilio en la historia de la Champions League. Y hay más. Tasos Douvikas, ex del Celta de Vigo por el que el Como pagó apenas 13 millones de euros, firmó un hat-trick y, con seis tantos en su estreno en la competición, se situó como máximo goleador por delante de Haaland. Pero eso no es todo. Según OPTA, es el segundo futbolista que consigue marcar en cada uno de los cuatro primeros partidos de su equipo en la historia de la UEFA Champions League -desde que la competición adoptó su actual denominación-, después de Alessandro Del Piero, que vio puerta en las cinco primeras jornadas de la edición 1995/96. En el minuto 58 llegó el turno de Mattia Liberali, una joya a la que el Como logró convencer para sumarse a su proyecto pese al interés del Milan, el club en el que se había formado. Apenas cuatro minutos después, gol y récord: con 19 años, seis meses y 29 días, Liberali se convirtió en el futbolista italiano más joven en marcar en la Champions League desde Mario Balotelli en 2009. Todo ello... hasta que entró en escena Matteo Papaccioli, nacido en 2008. Ya en el tiempo añadido, un pase filtrado perfecto de Liberali acabó en un gol de Papaccioli, que le arrebató el récord a su compañero apenas unos minutos después. De un italiano a otro. De un jugador del Como a otro. Y pensar que en Italia todavía hay quien critica a Cesc por no contribuir al desarrollo del fútbol nacional al no dar suficientes oportunidades a los futbolistas italianos... ¿Se acabó aquí? Ni mucho menos. También está Nico Paz, protagonista de otra exhibición, como si llevara toda la vida brillando en las grandes noches europeas. Con tres goles y cinco asistencias, es, por el momento, el futbolista que más participaciones directas en goles acumula en toda la Champions League. ¿El segundo? Anastasios Douvikas, con seis goles y una asistencia. Por delante de Kane, Yamal, Haaland y otras grandes estrellas del fútbol mundial. Un dominio absoluto de un club de una ciudad de apenas 80.000 habitantes que está disputando la competición por primera vez en su historia. Para el Como es su sexta victoria consecutiva. Y hay un detalle que no se puede pasar por alto si queremos poner todavía más en valor el extraordinario trabajo de Cesc Fàbregas: el equipo está en cuadro. Además de Chalobah, titular indiscutible en defensa, tiene de baja a más de la mitad de sus efectivos ofensivos: Assane Diao, Jesús Rodríguez, Jayden Addai y Moise Kean. Pero nada parece ser un problema para el técnico catalán, que se sacó de la manga una alineación con cuatro o cinco centrocampistas sobre el césped, todos capaces de intercambiar posiciones, atacar los espacios, asociarse en corto y marcar goles a raudales. El Como no es el mayor espectáculo del fútbol italiano. Por una noche, el Como ha sido el mayor espectáculo del fútbol europeo.

articles.title: Valdano matiza el "aceptable" de Mourinho sobre Vinicius: "No podía decir que hizo un partido pobre"
articles.standfirst: "Aceptable... dijo Mourinho. No podía decir que hizo un partido pobre Vinicius, pero la palabra aceptable no es tan elogiosa para un jugador totalmente desequilibrante"
articles.summary: "Aceptable... dijo Mourinho. No podía decir que hizo un partido pobre Vinicius, pero la palabra aceptable no es tan elogiosa para un jugador totalmente desequilibrante"
articles.body: Jorge Valdano, que fue jugador del Real Madrid de 1984 a 1987 y entrenador del equipo merengue de 1994 a 1996, analizó las palabras de Mourinho sobre el rendimiento de Vinicius en el partido que el Real Madrid remontó para acabar ganando 2-3 al AEK de Atenas en Champions League. "Vinicius ha hecho un partido muy aceptable, no extraordinario, como el equipo. Hay que pensar en el resultado, pero también en el Valencia. Por eso cambié a Diomande y Bernardo. Con Vini, hasta ahora 80% mano blanda y 20% dura", declaró el técnico luso sobre el jugador brasileño. Valdano habló en Movistar Plus Deportes sobre las palabras de Mou hablando de Vini. "Aceptable... dijo Mourinho. No podía decir que hizo un partido pobre Vinicius, pero la palabra aceptable no es tan elogiosa para un jugador al que tenemos representado como totalmente desequilibrante", apuntó el exfutbolista. Santiago Cañizares, que fue jugador del Real Madrid en dos etapas (1988 a 1992 y 1994 a 1998), también habló del rendimiento de Vinicius en el Real Madrid. "A Vinicius lo que peor le ha sentado es perder aquel Balón de Oro (el que ganó Rodri en 2024) y sentirse en una situación en que un club (Real Madrid) se pliega a él y no viaja a la gala del Balón de Oro. Son cosas que no son naturales, y que ahora Vini piensa que tiene un estatus, que contractualmente lo tiene...", apuntó el de Puertollano. Cañizares subrayó en 'La Casa del Fútbol' de Movistar Plus Deportes que "ahora tiene que pasar Mourinho a defender a Vinicius en cada rueda de prensa". "Vinicius es incapaz de defender ese estatus dentro del terreno de juego", sentenció.

articles.title: What Can Sunderland Expect From Croatian Champions Dinamo Zagreb?
articles.summary: Ahead of tonight’s match, we spoke to Croatian football writer, Lovre Nikolac, to find out what to expect.
articles.body:
Dinamo won both the Croatian league and cup last season under Mario Kovačević.

How would you reflect on that campaign and what were the expectations among supporters heading into this season?

Last season's campaign went about as well as Dinamo wanted after not winning anything the season prior; they dominated and returned to their usual form. They always want to win the domestic double; they essentially take it for granted. So the real challenges/expectations come in Europe, with them being back in the UCL qualifiers; the club and the fans want to return to the UCL. This didn't happen, as they lost to the Norwegian side, Viking, because of their poor defensive lapses in concentration, as they conceded two goals in quick succession in both legs. This left the fans mad at the higher-ups for not bringing in immediate improvements for the squad beforehand, and at the coach for the poor reactions from the team.

It's just the players' form; everybody except Dion Drena Beljo is struggling to play at a good level game after game. The defence, especially, has been the most inconsistent. Consistently losing their man or having poor reactions inside the box. Kovačević has tried to tweak a few things, with some changes to the starting XIs here and there, but nothing has clicked. Kovačević left the club by mutual consent just four days before the trip to Sunderland despite winning the double last season.

Were you surprised by that decision and do you think it was the right one?

Not surprised by the decision at all; it was a long time coming, as in September fans were already calling for his departure after really poor performances vs. Istra, Osijek and Hapoel Be'er Sheva. Even in victories, Dinamo were unconvincing and barely got them over the line, as they were put under serious pressure by Gorica and Lokomotiv, for example. I think it's the right decision, because at the end of the day, Kovačević has struggled a LOT and hasn't delivered after saying time and time again, "We need to improve next match," and that never happened. It seems like the pressure of a bad slump really got to him, since it's the first one he's had that is this bad. articles.title: The Régis Rebirth — Can Le Bris Find The Magic Formula For Sunderland?
articles.summary: Ben McKevitt looks at where the head coach might’ve erred this season and where he could make tweaks to help the Lads.
articles.body:
We've all seen how things have gone wrong over the last few days, weeks and months and a lot of errors could be attributed to Régis Le Bris over that period.

It looks like the club are backing Le Bris for at least a little bit longer in the hope that he can figure the whole mess out and get some points on the board. Whether you agree with the decision or not, I'm sure many of you have some opinions on how he should go about changing our fortunes, and I'm no different!

So, I thought it would be fun to have a look at some things he may consider to flip the script for the Lads in the coming weeks with the fair caveat that although I think these are fair points to raise, I believe that Le Bris is a truly gifted manager with more knowledge and experience of the game than I could ever hope to possess.

For that reason, I'll be offering some counters to each point for a bit of balance.

First up for me is to pick a style and to stick to it.

To my eyes, it looks like we have no clear sense of direction or intention in our play anymore. When we have the ball, we often pass it from side to side without incision. When we don't, we sit deeply without any quick players to counter incisively.

We've seemingly lost our patterns of play, our triangles and a clear way of moving through the thirds dangerously, and it looks like Le Bris is stuck between two styles at the moment.

Disregarding his first five or so games in charge wherein he employed a wonderfully intense press in the Championship, he's has generally and successfully set us up as a defensively solid team that's clinical in transition.

We recruited for this, as well — big defenders without much passing range, record signing Habib Diarra, whose primary attribute is carrying the ball at pace, and quick wingers that could hurt teams on the break. We soak up pressure and we punish teams for committing too much, or at least we used to.

To me, it looks like Le Bris has tried to evolve this style and introduce some more possession-based, expansive traits into our play over the last few months. You could see it starting ever since we breached our forty point target last season, and with a couple of slip-ups here and there, it was a smooth transition with impressive results.

Fast forward to the present day, though, and it's a mess, with a a slow and tedious attack, a dreadful defensive record and a non-existent midfield.

We're getting the worst of all worlds at the moment and I think that if Le Bris wants to succeed, he must bring it back to basics and introduce some pace for the counter or change tact altogether and find a different way for Sunderland to impose themselves on our opponents in the interests of chance creation.

Le Bris needs to commit to one style of play and stick to it in order to streamline and coordinate the players' thought processes on the pitch.

We've actually created more chances this year than last, but we're just not taking them.

Le Bris can't legislate for the players' inexplicable lapses in concentration and poor finishing while on the pitch, and perhaps the results are making the setup of the team look worse than it is.

I touched on this above but regardless of which style we're going to play going forward, we need to fix our disjointed, ineffective press.

If Coventry can play through us at a snail's pace while four or five of our players amble after them with no sense of cohesion, we're in trouble. This does link to the style of play, and I think it's one of the consequences of our seemingly ill-prepared gameplans — the lads are pressing individually rather than collectively and for me, that all comes down to the manager.

We didn't always press highly last season but if we did, it was "connected " and it was intense.

It's not just him, but a frequent and obvious example of this has been Granit Xhaka's floundering on his own in the opposition's box and leaving the defence hopelessly exposed.

It's been criminal and, at times, a bit jarring to watch the slow-motion car crashes we cause ourselves in this manner. Le Bris needs to resurrect the joined-up and well-drilled pressing machine, otherwise we're destined to sleepwalk into defeats regardless of our attacking play.

Tied in with the style of play, Le Bris needs to nail down our press so that it goes back to being confrontational, intense and cohesive.

Not much of a counter to this one, for me.

I can appreciate that the coaching staff haven't had many days on the training ground this season, but a team's press is a very good way to judge the cohesion of thinking and intent behind the scenes — in our case, shockingly absent at the moment.

This is a big one for me, as many players are getting an easy ride at the moment despite dropping stinker after stinker.

Xhaka's drop off in performance is well documented and while I'll talk about him a bit later on, there are a lot of other players who have let the side down consistently and with damaging consequences yet we know that every time a Premier League game comes back around, we're going to see all of the same faces again.

I'd name them here but if we're being honest, it's almost all of the starting XI from the most recent game against Coventry.

To compound the misery of the team selections, we've actually seen what the second string are capable of due to the sheer volume of games and the necessitation of rotation.

Jules Ahoka, Dayann Methalie, Malick Fofana, Jocelin Ta Bi and Habib Diarra (pre-re-injury) all deserve more minutes than they're getting — if nothing else but to inject some life into a slow and tired-looking group. As it is, we've ended up with a dysfunctional yet undroppable XI that works for nobody and rewards complacency from the core group while ignoring impressive displays from the unfavoured.

Le Bris must start shaking things up in the Premier League starting eleven.

Good performances from the second string shouldn't be ignored and bad performances from the starting XI (regardless of who's delivering them) shouldn't be rewarded with further starts.

Le Bris is sticking to his tried and tested approach on the pitch and wants to keep the two squads quite separate this early in the season. This means that we rotate heavily for cup games and leave as many fit and firing for both competitions as possible.

It also continues a trend we've always seen from Le Bris: play through bad form, but we just haven't needed to see it on this scale before.

This might be the most basic of the lot.

Le Bris seems to be actively shooting himself and the team in the foot by refusing to play with two wingers and/or full backs permitted to provide attacking support. Doing so would allow us to develop more threat on either flank by providing more space for wingers to cut in on their favoured foot or, alternatively, creating space for the full backs to put in a cross.

These are basic dynamics in football and something we've done under Le Bris before, so where have they gone?

Playing two right-footed full backs on the wing as was commonplace for months before Chris Rigg's introduction left us with a lopsided and slow attack. It's not much better with Rigg, either, as he's technically gifted and hard-working but not a specialised winger capable of pacey bursts at defenders.

We've seen what our wingers are capable of against Brentford in the League Cup, so to continue depriving ourselves of pace and creativity in the Premier League under the guise of defensive solidity is difficult to justify on our current form.

For me, it's critical that Le Bris finds a solution to this and it seems easy enough on paper.

Florent Ghisolfi has given him enough tools to figure something out on the wing, even if we didn't get that standout signing on the right.

Le Bris must find a way to improve our wing play as the current setups aren't giving us enough dynamism or threat in their current form.

Again, we're statistically creating more chances this season than last using these tactics.

Nordi Mukiele is often given heavy license to get past on the overlap which is often our most dangerous threat. Tactics involving midfielders or full backs in wide areas had worked last year in giving us more control of the game.

Protect Granit Xhaka in midfield and help Brian Brobbey

This could be a more contentious one, but I think we need to help ourselves more by covering for Xhaka's downturn in athleticism and dynamism.

I think we're often leaving him exposed in the middle of the park through a mixture of poor tactics, poor pressing and defensive calamities and if we can find a way to free Xhaka of needing to do as much of the dirty work as he used to, we just might find that he still has the quality we need to unlock defences. His play leading to Brobbey's ill-placed finish against Coventry shows that he has the vision when we give him the space he needs.

On this note, to me it's imperative that we give Brobbey more support in his isolated role as a hold-up striker.

I don't need to tell anyone how good he is in that role but it is ultimately fruitless when we don't have players playing off of him.

He's often left alone in twenty or thirty yards of space while the team slowly pushes up into the opposition half, let alone get near to him. The wingers and Noah Sadiki and Enzo Le Fée should be buzzing in and around him to pick up on his layoffs and if Le Bris can manage that, we'll start to reap more rewards from Brobbey's good work.

Support Xhaka's weaknesses and play to Brobbey's strengths.

Gaps in midfield and isolated forward lines are causing us issues in attack and defence.

Habib Diarra's injury has played a big part in both aspects, for me.

He covers the ground quickly and effectively while getting close to Brobbey in an attacking sense when we go forward. His presence — whether it's instead of Sadiki/Le Fée or in a different system altogether — could be a great solution if he can stay fit.

I'll also concede that while Xhaka has been exposed, he's also been a much less effective player generally this season — the causes of which we can't truly know.

articles.standfirst: Los de Bordalás quieren quitarse el mal sabor de boca de la goleada del Lugano
articles.summary: Los de Bordalás quieren quitarse el mal sabor de boca de la goleada del Lugano
articles.body: El Getafe buscará frente al Brighton un triunfo de renombre que le dé a los de Bordalás tres puntos que sirvan para encarrilar una Fase Liga de Conference League que se ha complicado tras las dos primeras jornadas. Tan solo un empate, frente al Craiova, y una derrota, contundente, frente al Lugano, es el bagaje de los del sur de Madrid, que quieren, de nuevo en casa, revertir esa situación y colocarse con cuatro puntos. Por su parte, el cuadro inglés, tercero en Premier League, llega después de vencer al FK Kauno Zalgiris por 4-0 y empatar a cero frente al Jablonec. Además, en liga aterrizan en el Coliseum tras vencer 0-1 al Manchester City y ser la revelación del campeonato inglés. Bordalás habló de la dificultad de saltar al campo a jugar después de conocer la muerte de Jesús de Miguel este martes: “Son momentos durísimos y muy difíciles. Ante una tragedia como esta, todo lo demás queda en un segundo plano. Intentamos seguir adelante porque la vida continúa y el equipo está trabajando, pero al final nosotros no somos quienes decidimos si se compite o no; veremos qué se determina. Obviamente estamos muy afectados y tristes. Es algo que no debería suceder y ha sido una desgracia tremenda”. Sobre el rival, advirtió a los suyos del potencial del equipo inglés: “Nos medimos a un grandísimo rival y estamos obligados a igualar su nivel de intensidad; de lo contrario, sufriremos, porque ellos cuentan con futbolistas de primer nivel que compiten en una de las ligas más potentes del mundo y marchan terceros por méritos propios. Debemos corregir de inmediato los desajustes a balón parado, ya que en los dos últimos compromisos nos penalizó encajar gol en esas acciones tempranas”. También habló Enes Ünal sobre el rival: “Cuentan con un plantel muy amplio y con futbolistas capacitados para rotar. Como bloque son muy completos: tremendamente intensos, compiten muy bien y ejecutan exactamente lo que exige cada partido. Son muy prácticos y saben manejar los tiempos a la perfección”.

articles.title: La Real, a seguir la remontada con el Lyon
articles.standfirst: El club txuriurdin y el francés se ven por quinta vez en Europa, con dos victorias para cada uno, teniendo el desempate de hoy mucho valor
articles.summary: El club txuriurdin y el francés se ven por quinta vez en Europa, con dos victorias para cada uno, teniendo el desempate de hoy mucho valor
articles.body: La Real Sociedad y el Olympique de Lyon se reencontrarán hoy en la Europa League después de haberse enfrentado en el siglo XXI en dos eliminatorias en la Champions a ida y vuelta, con dos victorias para cada equipo, por lo que los txuriurdin querrán desequilibrar ese balance a su favor para hacerse con tres puntos con los que superarían a los franceses en la clasificación y darían un paso adelante más hacia el top 8. La primera vez que Real y Lyon se midieron fue en los octavos de final de la Champions League 2003-04, con dos triunfos por la mínima de los Juninho, Diarra, Essien, Malouda y compañía. 10 años más tarde se iba a repetir el enfrentamiento en esta misma competición, en esta ocasión en la última ronda de clasificación para la fase de grupos y esta vez hubo dos triunfos txuriurdin por 0-2 y 2-0, con la icónica imagen del gol de chilena de Griezmann en la ida y el de Vela en la vuelta tras carrera de área a área. Como Pellegrino Matarazzo dijo antes del derbi, el pasado queda atrás y ahora se trata de escribir nuevas historias con distintos futbolistas a los cracks de aquellas dos eliminatorias, así que esta tarde será el turno de los Oyarzabal, Guedes, Óskarsson o Kubo, si, como parece, los cuatro tienen cabida en el equipo titular. En esa alineación inicial, todo indica que Unai Marrero volverá a ocupar la portería si el técnico de Nueva Jersey continúa con sus rotaciones habituales, con Aramburu, Jon Martín, Sarr y Sergio Gómez inamovibles en defensa, salvo que Fort, Zubeldia o Aihen tengan una oportunidad. Yangel Herrera y Turrientes pueden entrar en el doble pivote, con Oyarzabal por delante en la media punta y Óskarsson en ataque, teniendo ambos en los costados a Kubo, Barrenetxea o Guedes. La Real, con cuatro puntos tras las tres primeras jornadas, tras la imprescindible victoria en Lillestrom, ascendería algunas posiciones de salir vencedora de Anoeta, al pasar al menos a su rival de esta tarde y tener algunos otros clubes encuentros complicados, lo que supondría que podía acercarse un poco más a ese top 8 que persigue para evitar los dos partidos de la ronda de dieciseisavos. Esa misma meta tiene un Olympique de Lyon que llegará ‘tocado’ anímicamente, ya que cuando en la Ligue 1 era tercero, con sólo dos derrotas, una frente a un PSG al que plantó cara hasta casi el final, y en esta Europa League estaba al borde de los ocho primeros puestos, su técnico, Paulo Fonseca, ha decidido rescindir su contrato para marcharse al Sporting Portugal, movimiento hecho oficial ayer mismo. Jorge Maciel será su sustituto hoy en el banquillo de Anoeta. El delantero, autor de seis goles, Nuamah es baja y el veterano Corentin Tolisso ha encontrado el camino hacia portería, al marcar tres en los seis partidos más recientes. Greif, ex del Mallorca, es su portero.

articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Lo primero, el final: un cañonazo de Valverde valió el 2-3 sobre la hora, después del carrusel de cambios y en pleno arreón al estilo de Roma. Vino a ser la confirmación de algo tan viejo como el hilo negro: cuando el Madrid se pone serio se desata la galerna, y eso hay pocos que lo aguanten. Esta de anoche es la séptima victoria consecutiva del Madrid, buena racha. Le consolida en el top-8 y limpia una pequeña mancha en el historial. Ayer supe por el erudito Pedro Martín que de los 116 rivales que se ha echado a la cara el Madrid en Europa, sólo a tres no los había vencido. Uno de ellos era el AEK. Ya lo puede tachar. Sólo quedan Arsenal y Lille. Pero hecho eso, anotados los puntos y felicitado Valverde por su taponazo decisivo, queda lamentar que el Madrid no apretara hasta el final. Y enseguida la mirada se gira hacia Vinicius, al que Mourinho alineó de salida como parte de una visible intención de aprovechar este partido para repartir minutos. De hecho, Militao jugó el partido completo por primera vez en muchos meses. El reparto, claro, incluía a Vinicius, que ocupó su lugar en la izquierda desplazando a Diomande a la derecha, donde hizo cosas pero brilló menos. Menos aún brilló fue Vinicius, sin filo. Es difícil saber si le falta velocidad, confianza o las dos cosas, pero en cualquier caso también le falta lo que le faltó siempre, trabajo hacia atrás. Puede sonar lugar común, pero la verdad es que me quedó la impresión de que la buena dinámica de los últimos partidos se averió con su mera presencia. Mourinho no pudo ir en su análisis más allá de calificar su actuación como ‘muy aceptable’, lo que sonó a aprobado bajo. A la hora de los cambios quitó a Diomande antes, pero luego no tuvo más remedio que sustituirle para provocar ese electroshock, ya tradición madridista, que suele conducir a la victoria. Antes que Valverde habían marcado Bellingham, en un taconazo exquisito, y Mbappé, que siempre está. Courtois hizo las dos paradas iniciales de ritual. En fin, el Madrid. Con o sin Vinicius, ellos están ahí.

articles.title: En el último suspiro
articles.standfirst: Una opinión de Manuel Juliá
articles.summary: Una opinión de Manuel Juliá
articles.body: Cuando ya tenía el artículo medio hecho y rumiaba que ganábamos, los griegos clavaron uno por debajo de las piernas de Courtois. Quedaban catorce minutos. El Madrid iba perdiendo. En ese tiempo otras veces sacó la épica. En esta también. Una pistola humeante, sangre en el corazón enemigo y a los vestuarios. Este Madrid del último suspiro genera un sufrimiento que después se vuelve alegría. Así ganó algunas Champions. En el bar Juani se hizo el mismo montón de abrazos que en el campo. Los mismos gritos. Las mismas alegrías. El “pantallón” LG olía a yerba fresca y a columnas jónicas. Ganar así es dietético. No vas al servicio y bebes y bebes cerveza. Luego descargas a gusto. Facundo, el argentino dueño del bar Juani, es del Atlético. Cuando juega el Madrid ilumina una parte del bar y otra la deja en sombra. Y cuando va mal, nos suele decir, recordando viejos malos partidos, a ver qué Madrid vemos hoy, si el de las luces o el de las sombras. Lo dijo y enseguida marcó Mbappé. Hasta las gambas pegaron un grito de alegría. Con el empate estábamos tan atentos al “pantallón” que nos dimos cuenta de que Facundo y sus conmilitones estaban cerca del infarto. Luego llegó Valverde y la rompió entre las redes. Ese jodido uruguayo, dijo Facundo perdido entre las sombras mientras hasta los percebes saltaban de alegría. Todo el bar se hizo luz de repente. Empecé con el Barça. Ya me decía que pronto marcaría. Y que rápido vendría otro. Emigré hasta el Atlético que luchaba como un gladiador contra ese Bayern que nunca para de correr y apretar. Fuerza, calidad a raudales en ambos equipos, pero el Bayern será muy difícil de vencer. El Atlético dio todo, pero no fue suficiente para esa garra y talento alemán que es tan habitual desde no sé cuándo. Llegué al Villarreal que ya iba perdiendo. No recuerdo si por dos o tres goles. La máquina arrolladora de Luis Enrique estaba funcionando a tope. Me sentí mal cuando vi que salvo el Barça, nuestros equipos perdieron. Al Barça quiero verlo con los grandes equipos. De vez en cuando la muerte se asoma a un campo de fútbol y lo desordena todo. Cambia la alegría en tristeza. Cambia el viento azul en viento oscuro y deja una fría soledad en el corazón de los jugadores. En todos los campos se hizo el silencio. Sonó la música erizando el vello del cuerpo. Todos los jugadores bajaron la cabeza. Pensaron en él, en Jesús de Miguel Alameda, y sintieron un dolor que no tiene colores. Es la vida, el destino, el tiempo, el recuerdo. Esa desgracia duele por todas partes. El mundo del fútbol está triste porque falta Jesús. Tenía treinta años y una vida por delante. Mi más profundo pésame a todos los que le amaban y al fútbol.

articles.title: Mijatovic explica la resurrección de Valverde y advierte que "veo sufriendo" a Vinicius en el Madrid
articles.standfirst: "Creo que Vinicius necesita relajarse"
articles.summary: "Creo que Vinicius necesita relajarse"
articles.body: Pedja Mijatovic, jugador del Real Madrid de 1996 a 1999 y director de fútbol de equipo blanco de 2006 a 2009, analizó en 'El Larguero' la situación del Real Madrid tras ganar 2-3 al AEK de Atenas para sumar 12 puntos de 12 en Champions League. "Otra remontada más. Eso para los aficionados, las remontadas épicas, son muy bonitas. Pero yo preferiría vivir un partido tranquilo en el que el Real Madrid domine desde el minuto 1 hasta el 90' y no tener tanto estrés. Hoy, por ejemplo, empezamos muy mal... Vamos a vivir un poco más tranquilos, por favor, disfrutar al menos del fútbol. Menos remontadas y más tranquilidad", comentó el exfutbolista. Mijatovic habla en la SER de la gran 'resurrección' de Fede Valverde a las órdenes de Jose Mourinho: "Te voy a decir una cosa que todos los jugadores tienen siempre presente en la cabeza. Cuando un jugador de un equipo importante sabe que enfrente tiene un entrenador que ha conseguido todo y que tiene una gran personalidad, pero también el respaldo total del club, el jugador aceptará absolutamente todo. Pero todo. Si los jugadores tienen la duda de que el entrenador no tiene el respaldo del club, empiezan esas declaraciones: 'Yo puedo jugar aquí, pero no nací para esto...'. Cuando saben que el club respalda al entrenador, aceptan todo y quieren jugar... Vuelven a nacer, digamos. Eso lo he vivido yo, como futbolista y por eso te lo digo". "Mourinho está consiguiendo algo muy importante: los jugadores que juegan poco entran al campo contentos, con ganas y queriendo dejar su mejor versión. Y eso es clave por que la plantilla es amplia y a lo largo de la temporada vas a necesitar a todos", compartió con Manu Carreño. Pedja Mijatovic también opinó sobre uno de los grandes debates en el madridismo, como es el rendimiento de Vinicius: "La verdad es que viendo los partidos que ha hecho hasta ahora le veo sufriendo. Hasta ahora no tenía competencia y ahora sí, y eso se ve. Ahora está jugando con mucha presión, quiere ser decisivo en cada momento y está lejos de su mejor versión. Creo que necesita relajarse. Sigo diciendo que Vinícius tiene mucha temporada por delante y pensando en mejorar puede llegar a ser decisivo. Y si hay alguien que puede llevar este tema bien es Mourinho". "Con todo lo que ha pasado este verano lo puedo entender, pero una vez que has tomado la decisión de continuar (tras renovar hasta 2032), te tienes que olvidar de todo lo que ha pasado para centrarte en tu mejor versión. Pero yo sigo creyendo que nos puede dar muchas alegrías", comentó Mijatovic sobre Vinicius. Pedja Mijatovic subrayó el gran rendimiento que está teniendo Jude Bellingham en el Real Madrid. "Fantástico, para mí Bellingham hoy fue el mejor sobre el campo. Y no solo hoy, le estoy viendo muy bien en muchos partidos. Lo único que, como cuando llegó marcó tantos goles, la gente echa de menos esas cifras, pero él nunca ha sido un goleador. Pero Bellingham, lo que está haciendo en estos partidos, es lo que necesitamos de él. Y si además marca, como hoy, pues muchísimo mejor", compartió el de Pogdorica.

articles.title: Enzo Maresca’s Manchester City are trading control for chaos – and it could become the norm
articles.summary: Manchester City had one job to do against RB Leipzig at the Red Bull Arena last night. That was to leave Germany with all three points to aid their bid to se...
articles.body:
Manchester City had one job to do against RB Leipzig at the Red Bull Arena last night. That was to leave Germany with all three points to aid their bid to secure a top-eight finish in the UEFA Champions League league table. Enzo Maresca's side did exactly that as they picked up a 3-2 win over an impressive RB Leipzig outfit. Last night's match followed a familiar pattern of matches that City have played this season. It was an open affair where both teams had their chances to win. Watching the early stages of Enzo Maresca's reign as Manchester City manager, it does now seem like there is a pattern evolving which is far away from the control that anyone who has watched City over the past decade has become accustomed to.

Manchester City once again came out on top against RB Leipzig in a match that resembled a shootout.

At halftime of last night's match, Manchester City held a 1-0 lead. RB Leipzig defender Castello Lukeba turned a Nico O'Reilly cross into his own net in the 37th minute. The first half of last night's match wasn't the most inspiring viewing. However, that changed dramatically in the second half.

RB Leipzig took the game to Manchester City. Clearly Martin Demichelis had instructed his side to take the game to the visitors. They did exactly that. Led by Antonio Nusa, RB Leipzig threw everything at Enzo Maresca's side. They were rewarded with an equalizer in the 49th minute when Ridle Baku beat Gianluigi Donnarumma at his near post with a smart finish from a tight angle. City responded and restored their lead in the 58th minute when Enzo Fernandez headed home an Iliman Ndiaye cross. City's lead would only last three minutes when Antonio Nusa equalised for the hosts in the 61st minute. Erling Haaland would slide in an Elliot Anderson ball at the back post in the 78th minute to seal Manchester City's 3-2 win.

In the game's closing stages, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki both took shots that didn't pay off and gave RB Leipzig possession and an opportunity to surge forward in the final minutes of second half stoppage time. Rather than take the ball to the corner, they tried to seal a City win. In a way, that was indicative of how the second half played. Both teams could have won last night's match. However, now it seems that open and free-flowing games are becoming Manchester City's forte.

The control that became Manchester City's forte has been replaced with chaos.

For the decade that Pep Guardiola was Manchester City's manager, his team was determined to control matches. It was their modus operandi and formed the foundation of City's decade of success under Guardiola. Watching Pep Guardiola's Manchester City side control matches and ultimately strangle their opponents became common place. Now, under Enzo Maresca, City play in a completely different manner. The games feel more chaotic which has been seen throughout this season.

Manchester City's win over RB Leipzig followed a similar pattern to other games that City have played. City's 5-3 win over Sunderland and 3-2 win over Ipswich Town were both chaotic matches. As was Manchester City's 4-2 defeat to PSG. There is an openness to games that Manchester City are involved in. It was on display last night against RB Leipzig. Perhaps it is a sign of a squad that hasn't come together yet. Also, it appears that the way this City side is set up is conducive to open and free-flowing matches. Also, Manchester City's opponents aren't scared to go at the perceived weaknesses in their system.

All of these factors combined have seen a significant shift occur in matches that Manchester City are involved in. There is no doubt that Enzo Maresca does not want to be involved in shootouts as they were against RB Leipzig last night. However that is what is taking place currently.

It is jarring to see City play in so many chaotic matches after watching a decade of Pep Guardiola demanding his team control games. But this is a new era at City and while this team comes together and gels it may be a while yet before Manchester City control games as desried and have to continue to thrive in the chaos before the pattern changes.

articles.body:
They are the five individuals at the Premier League set to play a key role in the fate of Manchester City .

The competition's board has the responsibility of recommending a punishment after the seismic news in September of the club being found guilty of breaching financial rules by an independent commission.

While that three-person commission panel will ultimately decide on a sanction, the Premier League's submission will be considered, along with the view of City of course, who maintain their innocence and have appealed.

It is not known when a sanction hearing will take place, nor what sanction the Premier League will want, with a fine, points deduction, expulsion or the stripping of past titles all possible.

But who makes up the Premier League's board, and how have their recommendations over punishments been received in past disciplinary cases?

Among various roles and responsibilities, the board is the entity responsible for prosecuting breaches of Premier League rules.

It comprises the league's chair, chief executive, and three independent non-executive directors, with no club representatives included - in order to provide independence and neutrality.

Do Manchester City have any grounds to win their appeal?

How much did Man City's rule breaking cost your team?

Alison Brittain has kept a low profile since becoming the league's first female chair almost four years ago. Formerly a senior executive in the hospitality and financial services sectors, she is also chair and trustee of The King's Trust Group.

Described as "sensible" by one acquaintance, in September she spoke at a university alumni event, revealing that she was initially sceptical about joining the Premier League because she had never worked in sport.

Two senior club executives - the former Arsenal CEO Vinai Venkatesham (now at Spurs ), and ex- Aston Villa CEO Christian Purslow - told her that her skillset was what the league needed, helping to persuade her to apply.

She said: "They actually spent some time talking to me and saying 'we aren't looking for a super fan. In fact we're looking for the exact opposite - somebody who will bring a different mindset. A business mindset, governance standards, be able to reset us a little bit into a different way'…and so I then went through the process and ended up in the job."

Describing herself as a "lifelong Manchester United fan [who] stood in the Stretford End before it had seats, as a kid" because of her family's allegiance, Brittain is now also a Brentford supporter. In 2025, she received unanimous backing from the 20 clubs to continue for a second three-year stint.

Speaking in 2024, Brittain acknowledged the league was "not without its challenges". But she has hailed what she describes as "the most exciting competition in the world", and its global appeal, calling it an "enormous soft power asset" for the country.

She also recently said that "the whole point of running the league... is to make sure the competitive balance stays really good. Because what makes us successful is this virtuous circle of anyone could win any match any day… there has to be jeopardy."

She added: "Someone has to care about keeping that balance, because if you ask the clubs they'd rather not have that balance because they'd like to win all the time."

When asked if that was her job, she replied: "Absolutely. That's my job."

According to Purslow, Brittain has "extremely good people skills and diplomacy in a role where keeping 20 owners more or less happy is not an easy job. She is a very down to earth, straightforward person, and that plays well."

The league's chief executive since 2019, Richard Masters is a much more familiar face to football fans.

When the independent commission's 'core decision' on City was announced in September, he said it "vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case", and that the league has "a key responsibility… to ensure that the rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition".

He added that it was "paramount that the league remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously."

Masters said: "There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches. Now we have the commission's decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the league, our clubs and fans."

The board is completed with three other directors:

Mai Fyfield - a former Sky executive who during her 20-year career at the company led its bidding for three Premier League TV cycles, and currently sits on the board of BBC Commercial.

Dharmash Mistry - a technology venture capitalist and entrepreneur who also has experience of working with the BBC as a former non-executive director at the corporation. Describing himself as a "passionate football supporter", he is "smart and theoretical" according to one colleague. He chairs the Premier League's audit and finance committee and is the Premier League's representative on the FA's board.

Matthew Ryder - a senior barrister, part-time judge and a former deputy mayor of London when he had responsibility for social mobility and social engagement. He is also a board member of the Scott Trust, which owns the Guardian newspaper, alongside other non-executive roles. Describing himself as "a longstanding and passionate football fan", he also chairs the league's legal advisory group. He told a conference last year that his membership of the Premier League board had been "deeply rewarding... it's a fascinating time to be in football."

BBC Sport has approached the board members via the Premier League, but it declined to comment.

The Manchester City case is unique in its scale, and so it is uncertain how relevant previous cases are when looking at the kind of sanctions the Premier League has recommended. But it is clear that independent commissions do not necessarily agree with the Premier League's board when it comes to clubs' potential punishments.

In 2023, the league argued for a 12-point sanction for Everton after the club breached financial rules, with a commission then settling on a 10-point punishment instead, which was reduced to six points on appeal.

In 2024, the Premier League suggested that Nottingham Forest should be docked eight points over a larger PSR overspend, but the commission again disagreed, settling on a four-point punishment.

This year the Premier League argued that an appropriate sanction for Leicester City - for an overspend in 2023-24 - was a 12-point deduction to be applied in the Championship. The independent commission instead recommended that a six-point deduction be imposed by the EFL.

There is also an alternative to contested proceedings.

Earlier this year the Premier League board reached a 'sanctions agreement' with Chelsea which resulted in a £10m fine and suspended transfer ban after admitting making £47m in secret payments to unregistered agents and third parties over transfers between 2011 and 2018.

The league said: "When considering the appropriate sanction, the board noted that the club's proactive self-reporting, admissions of breach and exceptional co-operation throughout the investigation acted as significant mitigating factors."

articles.title: Toni Nadal: "¿Rafa presidente del Real Madrid? Eso es algo que va más allá de lo deportivo"
articles.standfirst: "Supongo que a mi sobrino Rafa le hará mucha ilusión ser directivo del Real Madrid, imagino que Florentino Pérez querrá escucharlo"
articles.summary: "Supongo que a mi sobrino Rafa le hará mucha ilusión ser directivo del Real Madrid, imagino que Florentino Pérez querrá escucharlo"
articles.body: Toni Nadal, tío y exentrenador de Rafa Nadal, se pronunció en 'Radioestadio Noche' de Onda Cero sobre el anuncio de que el extenista entrará en la Junta Directiva del Real Madrid. "Propuesta de la Junta Directiva de ratificación por la Asamblea General Extraordinaria de D. Rafael Nadal Parera como miembro de la Junta Directiva del Real Madrid C. F., de acuerdo con el artículo 46 de los Estatutos Sociales. En relación con dicho Orden del Día, la Junta aprobó por unanimidad someter a la aprobación de la Asamblea General Extraordinaria la siguiente propuesta: Ratificar el nombramiento de D. Rafael Nadal Parera como miembro de la Junta Directiva del Real Madrid C. F., de acuerdo con el artículo 46 de los Estatutos Sociales", anunció el Real Madrid. Toni Nadal compartió que "supongo que a mi sobrino Rafa le hará mucha ilusión ser directivo del Real Madrid; es algo que yo esperaba, es muy aficionado al club y quizá puede aportar aunque no sé qué función sería la suya, imagino que Florentino Pérez querrá escucharlo". "¿Rafael presidente del Real Madrid? No sé, no tengo ni idea; eso es algo que va más allá de lo deportivo", comentó. El tenista Carlos Alcaraz declaró que "lo de Rafa Nadal directivo del Real Madrid me parece una locura, me alegra por él". Rafa Nadal aceptó la propuesta para formar parte de la Junta Directiva del Real Madrid. "Quiero agradecer al presidente Florentino Pérez y a la Junta que me hayan propuesto entrar como parte de la Junta Directiva del Real Madrid", escribió Nadal en un mensaje con el que hizo pública su respuesta a la invitación para incorporarse al órgano directivo de la entidad blanca. "He aceptado esta propuesta con mucha ilusión, ganas de aprender y aportar todo lo que pueda", confirmó. El tenista comunicó su decisión a través de las redes sociales, donde agradeció la confianza de Florentino Pérez y expresó su ilusión ante esta nueva etapa vinculada al club.

articles.title: David Sánchez, sobre la llegada de Rafa Nadal a la directiva del Real Madrid: "Es un win-win de manual"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco considera que Florentino Pérez acierta con la incorporación del extenista
articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco considera que Florentino Pérez acierta con la incorporación del extenista
articles.body: David Sánchez lo tiene claro. La incorporación de Rafa Nadal a la directiva del Real Madrid sería todo un acierto para las dos partes. Así lo ha defendido en su opinión de este jueves en La Tribu de Radio MARCA, donde ha analizado las ventajas de la llegada del extenista al organigrama del club blanco. "La incorporación de don Rafael Nadal Parera a la directiva del Real Madrid es un win-win de manual por todas las partes", ha asegurado. El periodista considera que el movimiento también sería positivo para el propio Nadal, que tendría la oportunidad de involucrarse en la gestión del club de sus amores: "Como madridista tendría ganas de trabajar y darle algo de su tiempo al equipo de sus amores". Para el Real Madrid, Sánchez encuentra tres grandes beneficios. El primero, el reconocimiento que despierta la figura del balear entre los aficionados: "Incorporas a un tío que aglutina, que es querido y, sobre todo, muy respetado por todo el madridismo". El segundo tiene que ver con la renovación de los órganos de gobierno: "Modernizas y rejuveneces una junta directiva que lleva muchos años al frente de la gestión del club". El tercer argumento apunta directamente al escenario electoral del conjunto blanco. "Da la sensación de que se lo quitas a la candidatura de Enrique Riquelme", ha señalado Sánchez, recordando que Nadal fue vinculado con él en las últimas elecciones a la presidencia del Real Madrid. Por todo ello, el periodista no ha dudado en elogiar el movimiento de Florentino Pérez: "En este caso también acierta Florentino Pérez. Win-win, repito, de manual". Eso sí, David Sánchez ha cerrado su reflexión con una incógnita sobre las responsabilidades que asumiría el extenista dentro del club: "Ahora falta saber el papel que va a desempeñar. Como embajador, matrícula de honor. Como gestor, tiene mucho tiempo para aprender".
